small_guidance:
- Output is stored as bf16 but the reference returns fp32; storing fp32 directly (and skipping the bf16 cast on output) avoids extra rounding work. Also try keeping output bf16 but verify correctness margin — the current 0.897 ms includes a bf16 cast of x every forward. Pre-cast x once or fuse cast into the kernel by loading fp32 x and casting inside (`x.to(tl.bfloat16)` after load) so the input copy elision kicks in.
- Add larger-K configs (BLOCK_K=256) and try `num_stages=5` for K=8192; with BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 the inner loop runs 128 iters — bigger BLOCK_K reduces loop overhead and improves pipelining on sm_89.
- Since M=N=K are all multiples of 128, drop the `% M`/`% N` masking on offs_m/offs_n (use plain offsets) and remove tail masks on the store — saves predicate compute in the hot loop.
large_guidance:
- Move the bf16 weight cast and (optionally) the x cast outside per-call cost: keep `w_bf16` as today (already done) but eliminate the per-forward `x.to(bfloat16)` allocation by writing a kernel that loads fp32 x and casts to bf16 register-side before `tl.dot`, removing a full M*K read+write each call (~32MB).
- Consider an fp16 path instead of bf16 on Ada (RTX 4090) — fp16 tensor cores have the same throughput but the accumulator/cast pipeline is sometimes better tuned; or try a TF32 fp32×fp32 `tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)` path to skip casts entirely.
- Try a persistent / split-K kernel: with M=1024, N=8192, K=8192 there are only 1024*8192/(128*128)=512 tiles, which under-occupies the 128 SMs of the 4090 only slightly, but a Stream-K or split-K (K split by 2-4) could improve SM utilization and L2 reuse on the K loop.
